chapter_title: Day 2: Byzantine Constantinople and Hagia Sophia
learning_objective: The learner will apply the rule "a thing belongs to the layer in which it arrived at this place" to assign twelve things seen on Day 2 to one of five historical layers, assigning at least 10 of 12 correctly on the first attempt.
specification:
Type: microsim **sim-id:** read-the-ruin-layers
**Library:** p5.js
**Status:** Specified
**Bloom Level:** Apply
**Bloom Verb:** classify
**Learning Objective:** The learner will apply the rule "a thing belongs to the layer in which it arrived at this place" to assign twelve things seen on Day 2 to one of five historical layers, assigning at least 10 of 12 correctly on the first attempt. **Prerequisites:** layers of a city, spolia, the four ways a layer is added (built over, reused, converted, removed), and the eras Roman, Byzantine, Ottoman and Republic (defined in Part Two, "Layers of a City", and in Chapter 1). **Evidence of Mastery:** For each card, the learner places it in one of the five layers before feedback. A placement is correct when it matches the Correct layer column in Content. Mastery is 10 of 12 correct on the first attempt, including at least 2 of the 3 cards marked "trap" (cards 2, 3 and 9), which are the ones where the object is much older than its arrival. **Misconceptions:** (1) An object belongs to the era in which it was made (cards 2, 3 and 9 expose this). (2) Anything that looks European and modern must be from the Republic (card 8 exposes this). (3) Removal is not a layer (cards 4 and 5 expose this). (4) Everything in Hagia Sophia is Byzantine (cards 10 and 11 expose this). **Instructional Rationale:** Placing real objects into layers under one explicit rule is an Apply task: the learner uses a procedure on new cases. The trap cards make the learner choose between the made date and the arrival date, which is where most visitors go wrong. **Content:** The five layers, each with its date range and one-line description: - Roman (before 330 CE): the city before Constantine's capital. - Byzantine (330–1453, except 1204–1261): the Christian imperial capital. - Latin occupation (1204–1261): rule by the crusaders and Venice after the Fourth Crusade. - Ottoman (1453–1922): the sultans' capital. - Republic (1923–today): the Turkish Republic. The rule, shown at the top throughout: "A thing belongs to the layer in which it arrived at this place, or, for a removal, the layer in which it was taken away." | # | Card | Made | Arrived or happened here | Correct layer | Reason shown after answering | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | The long, narrow shape of Sultanahmet Square | about 203 CE | about 203 CE | Roman | It follows the racetrack begun under Septimius Severus, before Constantine's capital. | | 2 | Obelisk of Thutmose III (trap) | about 1450 BCE, Egypt | raised here in 390 CE | Byzantine | Carved in ancient Egypt, but raised in the Hippodrome by Theodosius I in 390. | | 3 | Serpent Column (trap) | 479 BCE, Delphi | brought by 330 CE | Byzantine | Cast at Delphi after Plataea, but brought here when Constantine built his capital. | | 4 | Bare stone of the Walled Obelisk | 10th-century restoration | bronze plates stripped 1204 | Latin occupation | The bare stone is the trace of a removal by Fourth Crusade soldiers. | | 5 | Burial place of Enrico Dandolo, Doge of Venice, in Hagia Sophia's gallery | 1205 | 1205 | Latin occupation | The Venetian leader of the Fourth Crusade was buried in the church in 1205; the inscribed slab seen today is a later marker. | | 6 | Hagia Sophia's main dome | 562 | 562 | Byzantine | Rebuilt by Isidore the Younger after the first dome collapsed in 558. | | 7 | Mosaic of the Virgin and Child with Emperor John II Komnenos and Empress Irene | about 1122 | about 1122 | Byzantine | Made for the emperor and empress during the Komnenian dynasty. | | 8 | Octagonal German Fountain in the Hippodrome | 1900 | 1900 | Ottoman | A gift of Kaiser Wilhelm II to Sultan Abdülhamid II, before the Republic. | | 9 | Medusa heads under two columns in the Basilica Cistern (trap) | Roman, date unknown | 532 CE | Byzantine | Roman carvings reused as column bases when Justinian built the Cistern. | | 10 | Large calligraphic roundels naming God, the Prophet Muhammad and the first caliphs | about 1850 | about 1850 | Ottoman | Painted by the calligrapher Kazasker Mustafa İzzet Efendi after the Fossati restoration. | | 11 | Ablution fountain in Hagia Sophia's courtyard | 1740 | 1740 | Ottoman | Built for Sultan Mahmud I so worshippers could wash before prayer. | | 12 | Walkways and lighting in the Basilica Cistern | 2017–2022 | 2022 | Republic | Added in the earthquake-strengthening restoration, reopened in 2022. | **Provenance:** Cards 1 to 4, 6 and 8 come from Part Two, "Layers of a City"; card 5 from Part Seven, "The Fourth Crusade"; card 7 from Part Four, "Mosaic"; cards 9 and 12 from Part Five; cards 10 and 11 from Part Four, "Hagia Sophia" and its photos. Dates follow standard references (Wikipedia articles on each monument). **Rules:** Each card is placed once for scoring. A first-attempt placement is correct if and only if it equals the Correct layer. Score is 0 to 12; mastery is score >= 10 with at least 2 of the 3 trap cards correct. Cards appear in a fixed shuffled order with seed 4, the same for every learner. **Learner Activity:** 1. The learner reads the rule and the five layer descriptions. 2. The learner places a card in a layer. 3. Feedback shows the Made and Arrived dates and the reason; the card settles into its correct layer. 4. After all twelve cards, the learner sees the finished layer stack, with the count of cards in each layer (Roman 1, Byzantine 5, Latin occupation 2, Ottoman 3, Republic 1). 5. The learner should notice that the Byzantine layer holds three objects much older than Byzantium. **Feedback:** After each first attempt: correct shows "Correct" and the reason; incorrect shows "This one arrived in [correct layer]: [reason]". After card 12: if mastery is met, "You read the ruin. Try the same rule on the Library of Celsus at Ephesus on Day 7."; otherwise, "Look again at the trap cards: ask when each arrived, not when it was made." A Try Again option repeats the same twelve cards in a new order. **Starting State:** Five empty layers stacked from Roman at the bottom to Republic at the top, the rule, and card 1, with the question "In which layer did this arrive?" **Chapter Anchors:** Hippodrome begun about 203 CE; obelisk carved about 1450 BCE and raised in 390 CE; Serpent Column from 479 BCE; Walled Obelisk stripped in 1204; dome rebuilt 562; Komnenos mosaic about 1122; German Fountain 1900; Cistern built 532 and reopened 2022; Fossati restoration 1847–1849; ablution fountain 1740; twelve cards; mastery 10 of 12.
